synopsis: The glossary includes multilevel splitting in the booklet’s rare-event methods family; Chapter 9 describes these methods as oversampling dangerous conditions while estimating naturalistic rates, subject to observation-level reweighting [f14161, f6846]. Multilevel splitting and subset simulation originate in reliability engineering, specifically structural reliability, and can estimate rates through conditional levels [f6855, f7272, f7270]. Chapter 9 recommends them primarily for very small probabilities in structural reliability and identifies academic tools as typical tooling [f7269, f7273]. Although the methods have an independent evidence base, no collision-avoidance application or evidence was found, and discontinuous perception responses are an identified weakness [f7274, f6857, f6856, f7271].

relations.note: Adds oversampling and reweighting requirements to the glossary’s rare-event methods family.
Both report no collision-avoidance evidence; the latter also notes an independent evidence base.
Both identify weakness for discontinuous perception responses.
Both describe reliability origins, with structural reliability the more specific formulation.
Specifies conditional levels as the rate-estimation mechanism for these two methods.
Structural-reliability origins support the recommended application domain.
Perception-response weakness reinforces the recommendation to favor structural-reliability applications.
